item.title: December 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
Your Story Is Part of Our 40-Year Journey

For four decades, our community has been at the heart of our mission to create a more vibrant, beautiful Columbus. Thanks to thousands of volunteer hours rooted in shared passion and civic pride, we've kept our city a place we are all proud to call home.

As we celebrate this milestone year in 2026, we invite you to share your favorite memories, whether from a cleanup, a workshop, a beautification project you loved, or even a small but meaningful moment spent connecting with neighbors. Your stories bring to life what our organization stands for: a thriving, connected, and beautiful city.

Share your memories by February 1, 2026. We can’t wait to hear from you.

Submit your memories

Volunteer Spotlight: Lisa Boggs And Her 100th Lunchtime Cleanup

Lisa Boggs is just one cleanup away from completing her 100th lunchtime neighborhood litter collection.

Nearly every Friday, Lisa has led a weekly cleanup in her Hilltop community that brings neighbors together to care for their shared environment. Her commitment has inspired countless volunteers, strengthened community bonds, and made a visible difference across the community.

Lisa’s passion and perseverance embody the spirit of service at the heart of our mission. Her Friday cleanups have become a weekly tradition rooted in pride, teamwork, and love for our city.

Congratulations, Lisa, and thank you for your remarkable dedication to keeping Columbus beautiful.

Reminder: Volunteer Award Nominations Are Still Open!

There’s still time to recognize an outstanding volunteer, group, or partner through the KCB Volunteer Awards Recognition Program. Please help us honor the individuals and teams who make Columbus cleaner, greener, and more beautiful.

Nomination Deadline: January 9, 2026

Eligible Activities: Must have taken place in 2025

Award Categories:

  • Outstanding Adopt-An-Area Partner
  • Volunteer Group of the Year
  • Volunteer of the Year
  • Partner of the Year
  • Lifetime Achievement Award (Celebrating 40 Years)

Nominate someone here

A Meaningful Way to Give Back This Winter

The holiday season reminds us of the importance of giving back. If you, your family, company, or organization is looking for a meaningful way to make a difference this winter, consider joining our Adopt-An-Area program.

Through this program, participating groups help keep Columbus streets and public spaces clean and litter-free. It’s an excellent way to show civic pride, strengthen community connections, and make a visible impact in your community and at work.

Adopting groups receive:

  • Free cleanup supplies
  • Project guidance
  • Support with trash collection

Learn More About Adopt-An-Area

item.title: November 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
Volunteer Awards Recognition

We are excited to announce that nominations are now open for the annual Keep Columbus Beautiful Volunteer Awards Recognition Program! Each year, we honor the exceptional individuals and organizations who help advance our mission to keep Columbus clean, green, and beautiful.

We invite you to nominate someone whose dedication, leadership, and impact deserve to be celebrated.

📝 Nomination Deadline: January 9, 2026

🏆 Awards Presented: At the Keep Columbus Beautiful Volunteer Award Ceremony. Stay tuned for a save the date and special invitation!   

All volunteer activities must have occurred in 2025 to be eligible.

Award Categories

🌿 Outstanding Adopt-An-Area PartnerFor volunteers have been fully committed to their adopted area and make making a noticeable difference.

👥 Volunteer Group of the YearFor teams that brought great energy, teamwork, and impact this past year.

🌟 Volunteer of the YearFor the individual who went the extra mile in 2025 for a clean Columbus.

🤝 KCB Partner of the YearFor an organization that has shown strong, ongoing support for our mission beyond a one-time contribution.

🏅 Lifetime Achievement Award – Celebrating 40 Years of Keep Columbus BeautifulA special honor for someone who has been deeply committed to achieving a clean and green Columbus and inspiring others over many years.

Help us recognize the people who make our city shine. We can’t wait to celebrate them!

Nominate Someone Today! 

America Recycles Day – Community Cleanup Highlights

Keep Columbus Beautiful joined communities across the nation in celebrating America Recycles Day on November 15, partnering with the Columbus Crew, the Franklinton Board of Trade, Rumpke Waste & Recycling, and Avondale Elementary School for a neighborhood cleanup in Franklinton. Volunteers worked together to remove litter, promote recycling, and highlight the importance of environmental stewardship. We are grateful to our partners and community members whose teamwork and dedication help create a cleaner, greener Columbus.

Recycled Printmaking Workshop Recap

In November, Keep Columbus Beautiful partnered with Franklin Park Conservatory to host a hands-on recycled printmaking workshop where participants explored creative reuse by turning discarded Tetra Pak cartons into printing plates. We used a pasta press to create our prints, and participants engraved their designs using simple tools like pencils, pens, and X-Acto knives before inking and hand-printing their artwork. It was a fun, accessible way to connect sustainability with artistic expression. Thank you to everyone who joined us, and to Franklin Park Conservatory for collaborating to make this eco-friendly event a success!

item.title: October 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
City Employee Fall Cleanup

Over 200 City of Columbus employees spent a combined 522 hours picking up litter across the city during the annual Fall City Employee Cleanup earlier this month. Teams from numerous departments including The Mayor’s Office, Public Service, Water and Power, Public Health, Civil Service, Development, Neighborhoods, Human Resources, Recreation and Parks, and more, collected a total of 17,040 pounds of litter in public spaces. That’s heavier than an elephant! Interested in organizing a cleanup in your community? Sign-up here!

Pumpkins, Yard Signs, and Holiday Lights!

There is no need to trash those pumpkins, yard signs, or holiday lights! Drop them off at one of two Columbus Division of Refuse Collection Waste and Reuse Convenience Centers. In November, the Convenience Centers will accept pumpkins that are free of paint and markers for composting. They are located at located at 2100 Alum Creek Dr., and 1550 Georgesville Rd. and are open Tuesday through Saturday from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

Pumpkins can also be dropped off at the Stephen R. Lennon Refuse Collection Station, 4260 Morse Rd., Monday through Friday in November and two Saturdays, Nov. 1 and No. 29, 8 a.m. to noon.

In addition, the Convenience Centers will accept cardboard, paper, and plastic yard signs and metal wire stands, such as campaign signs, in November. Paper and cardboard signs may be placed in residents’ blue recycling containers, but plastic signs and metal wires should not be.

Holiday lights may also be brought to the Convenience Centers to be recycled with e-waste.

Tree Giveaway with Green Columbus

For the third year, the Keep Columbus Beautiful team joined dozens of volunteers to help deliver hundreds of trees with Green Columbus. From their tree nursery in Linden to Franklinton and the South Side, these trees were distributed to residents to help grow and increase the city’s tree canopy. Learn more about Green Columbus and their tree giveaway program here.

AmeriCorps Scioto River Cleanup

The Franklin Soil and Water Conservation District's new AmeriCorps cohort braved the rain to pick up litter at Scioto Audubon Metro Park for Stormwater Awareness Week in early October. The team prevented a lot of litter from being swept away in the rising river water. Efforts like this help prevent the estimated 52% of litter that pollutes our waterways. Organize a cleanup with us!

item.title: September 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
Game Over—Columbus Litter League 2025 Seasons Comes to an End

The totals for the 2025 Columbus Litter League season are in, and the winners are who collected the most bags of litter in each category are: 

  1. Keep It Clean (individual team) - 875 bags
  2. LYFE Savers (nonprofit team) - 498 bags
  3. Southern Orchards Cleanup Crew (community team) - 155 bags
  4. Team Huntington Bank (corporate team) - 91 bags

Combined, the 27 Litter League teams collected 2,585 bags of litter during the 2025 season, for an impressive 77,550 pounds of litter. This season included seven more teams than last year and 21,285 more pounds of litter. It's a real home run for Columbus! Thank you to the Columbus Clippers and Rumpke Waste & Recycling for supporting our players in this three-month summer competition!

Scioto Sweep Fishes Out Thousands of Pounds of Trash

Our annual Scioto River cleanup was held on Sept. 22 with 122 volunteers collecting over 3,950 pounds of litter from the waterway and shores.

Boosted by over 268 hours of human-power and partners from Green Columbus, the Scioto Watershed Action Group, Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, and more, this event makes a significant impact to keep our river clean and beautiful. These efforts help to ensure we contribute to reducing the estimated 52% of litter that is in our waterways across America. Thank you to all who participated!

Keep America Beautiful Podcast

On the most recent episode of Do Beautiful Things, a podcast hosted by Keep America Beautiful, Mayor Andrew J. Ginther is the featured guest. He discusses many of our city’s Refuse Collection collection programs including two Waste and Reuse Convenience Centers, the nine food scraps drop-off sites, weekly recycling collection, and of course, Keep Columbus Beautiful. The full episode can be found here or on your podcast platform of choice.

Trash Party

On Saturday, Sept. 6, volunteer-led group Trash Party headed to Wilson Road Park for a cleanup they helped  organize. In just a few hours, dozens of volunteers collected over 100 bags of trash and a few bulk items, like shopping carts and discarded furniture. Trash Party's cleanup resulted in more than 2,200 pounds of trash now removed from our community, bringing their total amount of litter collected over numerous cleanups to 37,000 pounds.

Organize a cleanup with us!

item.title: Join the Scioto Sweep on Sept. 21
item.description:
Did you know that 52% of all litter is found in our waterways? This litter harms wildlife, pollute our water, and make our waterways unsightly. Byvolunteering to clean up the Scioto River, you can help make a difference in community.

Join us on Sunday, September 21 at 10am to clean up the Scioto River at the annual Scioto Sweep! Keep Columbus Beautiful, in partnership with Green Columbus and the Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, is calling on all volunteers to take care of our environment. 

We will have all the supplies you need including gloves, trash bags, and litter grabbers. You can choose from 3 different locations including Scioto Audubon Metro Park located at 400 W. Whittier Street, Columbus, Ohio 43215. Register here! 

Be sure to wear closed-toe shoes. You may also want long pants if you plan to walk into the brush. Volunteers under the age of 18 must be accompanied by an adult.

We look forward to seeing you there!

item.title: August 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
Scioto Sweep 2025

Save the date for the Scioto Sweep 2025 on Sunday, Sept. 21.

Join Keep Columbus Beautiful, Green Columbus, Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, Scioto Watershed Action Group, and community partners for the annual Scioto Sweep. All supplies will be provided (including a limited number of kayaks) to remove trash, tires, and debris from the Scioto River and its banks. Whether you’re knee-deep in the water or helping along the shoreline, your time, and work will directly benefit wildlife, water quality and the neighbors we share.

Sign up, bring closed toe shoes, wear clothes that you can get dirty, and be ready to have a great time cleaning the river!

Learn more!

LifeCare Alliance Partnership

Keep Columbus Beautiful is partnering with LifeCare Alliance to help divert usable items from the landfill and provide them to seniors and others in need throughout Central Ohio. LifeCare Alliance serves thousands across Central Ohio through programs like Meals on Wheels, Cancer Support Services, and Community Wellness Centers.

They collect items such as toasters, canes, rollators, microwaves, and other small appliances that often end up as scrap metal because Goodwill and electronics recycling cannot accept them. Now, when these items are in working condition and brought to the city's Waste and Reuse Convenience Centers, they will be cleaned, checked, and ready for reuse instead of disposal.

Your donations help extend these essential services, providing comfort, safety, and dignity to seniors and others in need. Visit the LifeCare Alliance website to learn more about the great work they do. We are proud to be partners in their efforts supporting Central Ohio residents.

LifeCareAlliance

Third Annual Shiseido Employee Cleanup

Our third annual cleanup at Three Creeks Metro Park with employees of Shiseido was a success! Hundreds of team members joined in to clean up the park, creeks, and shorelines around the confluence of the Big Walnut, Alum, and Blacklick Creeks. Thanks to our partnership with Green Columbus, this effort continues to have a lasting impact on our waterways throughout Central Ohio. 

Interested in hosting a corporate clean up with us? Drop us an email!

The Next Generation of Green

The future is bright in Columbus, and it is in the hands of our youth. At Keep Columbus Beautiful, we believe that engaging youth is one of the most powerful ways to build a cleaner, more sustainable city.

Keep Columbus Beautiful provides complementary youth education programs for classrooms, youth clubs, day camps, afterschool activities, community organizations, and more! These educational services cater to students of all ages, from elementary to high school. The programming aligns with learning standards and is customized to meet the specific needs of your group, including a variety of activities such as workshops, presentations, lessons, and more.

item.title: July 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
Keep Columbus Beautiful Youth Program Makes News

A Keep Columbus Beautiful creative lesson on sustainability in a summer youth program at the Whitehall Branch of the Columbus Metropolitan Library was showcased in a recent NBC4 story.

Keep Columbus Beautiful worked with participants to make “Cork Boats” art out of garbage, and how to properly sort trash for recycling and composting.

The ultimate lesson is teaching kids that waste reduction and sustainability are lessons and habits they can carry with them their whole lives.

Watch Here

How Columbus is Moving the Needle on Waste Diversion

Check this out: Recorded live at the Midwest Regional Sustainability Summit, leaders from Columbus share how they’re building a more circular and equitable approach to waste diversion. Aryeh Alex (Keep Columbus Beautiful), Christy Walters (Columbus Greenspot), and Marcus Carano (Smart Columbus) dive into practical solutions—from food rescue pilots and mattress recycling to IT reuse and green job creation. Proving that sustainability isn’t just about reducing waste, but about creating opportunities. The conversation highlights how public policy, grassroots engagement, and cross-sector partnerships can align to drive real, lasting impact.

Listen to the recording here!

Coca-Cola Rain Barrels

Our third annual rain barrel workshop and giveaway was another huge success with over 100 residents receiving an upcycled syrup barrel. Thank you to Coca-Cola Consolidated for helping to bring this program to fruition with conversion kits, lunch, and support in organizing the event. The program not only helps reuse a material but also helps save water across our community. Follow our social media for details later this year about next year's event. 

Help Columbus Achieve its Climate Action Plan Goals

Four years after introducing the Columbus’ Climate Action Plan, Sustainable Columbus is updating the plan and wants your feedback on how you think our community's climate actions should be prioritized—including for reducing waste. To participate, you can fill out this survey to help Sustainable Columbus better understand what climate efforts matter most to you. The city remains committed to its ambitious goals, including a 45% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030.

Jazz & Rib Fest Food Rescue Another Success

For the second year in a row, staff from the Department of Public Service, Keep Columbus Beautiful, Columbus Public Health, and Columbus Food Rescue partnered to help save over 800 pounds of food at the conclusion of this year’s Jazz & Rib Fest—ensuring it fed people instead of the landfill. Columbus Food Rescue then delivered the rescued ribs, beans, slaw, macaroni, and raw ingredients to nine social service organizations in the city. Efforts like this show the importance of collaboration and community to address food waste, food insecurity, and climate change. Huge thanks to the donating vendors and all those who helped make the second year of this rescue operation a success!

item.title: June 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
New Supply Request & Event Summary Forms

We’re excited to launch two new tools to better support our volunteers and streamline our operations:

  • Supply Request Form – Makes it easier to request cleanup supplies and helps us track community impact more accurately.
  • Event Summary Form – Allows you to quickly report results and share highlights after your cleanup event.

To help you get started, we’ll host a webinar on July 1 from 1 to 2 p.m. to walk through how to use both forms. The session will be recorded and shared for anyone unable to attend live.

Use this link to join us and help us keep Columbus beautiful, efficient, and effective!

Staff Spotlight!

Check this out: Our very own Executive Director Aryeh Alex is featured in the summer issue of Ribbit! Magazine! Dive into the story on page 20 and learn more about the work we're doing to Keep Columbus Beautiful: https://ribbitmagazine.com/flipbook/

Columbus Litter League

We're on a mission to make our community cleaner and more beautiful this summer, and we want you to be a part of it. Join us in the Columbus Litter League—a fun and meaningful way to give back to our shared environment!

The Columbus Litter League isn't just about cleaning up—it's a fun, citywide competition that brings teams together to make a visible impact. Whether you're a first-time volunteer or a seasoned cleanup pro, this is a great way to connect with your community and protect the places we love.

How Does It Work? Teams compete by collecting litter in designated areas throughout Columbus. Each cleanup effort earns points, and the team with the most points at the end of the season wins! Players will also receive tickets to select Columbus Clippers games throughout the season. Litter League runs through August 31. Every bag of litter we pick up contributes to a cleaner, greener, and more beautiful Columbus.

Join the Litter League

Adopt-an-Area with Us

Seeking a distinctive way for your organization to engage, foster community connections, and preserve Columbus’ ecosystem? Check out Adopt-an-Area! This month, we're welcoming new Adopters, the Hayden Run Trail Society

We extend our heartfelt thanks to the South Eastmoor Civic Association, which demonstrated its commitment by removing 420 pounds of litter recently from its Adopt-an-Area location. Your dedication and hard work are commendable, and we appreciate your efforts in caring for our shared community.

item.title: May 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
The Columbus Litter League Is Back

Registration is now open Season 5! Opening Day is June 1, and we seek volunteers from across the city to form teams to help tackle litter in Columbus neighborhoods.

Teams will compete in one of the following categories:

  • Business/Corporation
  • Nonprofit or Faith-Based Organization
  • Community Group
  • Family/Individual
  • Youth Group (NEW this year!) — This exciting new division gives schools, scout troops, youth clubs, and student organizations a chance to get involved and make a real impact.

Thanks to Rumpke Recycling, our new sponsor, and our longtime supporters, the Columbus Clippers, every team member actively participating will be invited to attend Litter League Team Nights at select Clippers home games. The Litter League team with the most runs by collecting the most bags of litter by the end of the season will get the opportunity to meet Clippers players at Huntington Park, and one lucky team member will throw out the first pitch at a game September! This Litter League season runs from June 1 to August 31. 

Register Your Team

April Sets Record for Litter Cleanup and Volunteer Impact

April 2025 was a record-breaking month for Keep Columbus Beautiful, thanks to the dedication of our incredible volunteers and community partners! Together, we hosted 131 cleanups with 2,228 volunteers contributing 4,768.5 hours of service—valued at an astounding $151,638. These efforts resulted in the removal of 93,960 pounds of litter from our neighborhoods, the highest amount ever collected in an April. In addition, we participated in five community events, reaching 1,481 residents through our attendance and outreach. Thank you to everyone who helped make this a historic month of impact!

Have you seen an area in your neighborhood that needs cleaning up? Learn more and organize one here.

Community Dog Walk & Litter Clean-Up

Keep Columbus Beautiful is partnering with the Franklin County Dog Shelter a second time for a heartwarming and impactful community event! Take a shelter dog for a walk and help pick up litter along the way—it’s a win for the pups and the planet.

This unique volunteer opportunity combines pet adoption awareness with environmental stewardship. Whether you're looking to give back, enjoy some fresh air, or perhaps meet your future furry friend, we’d love to have you join us! Please register using this link.

item.title: March 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
Join Keep Columbus Beautiful and Green Columbus this Earth Month as we celebrate our planet and work together to protect its beauty for future generations.

Throughout April, we will host a series of engaging events, impactful cleanups, and educational programs to promote sustainability and environmental stewardship throughout our community.

Join or host a cleanup

2025 Cleaner Columbus Citywide Cleanup

Mark your calendars for Saturday, April 5, 9 a.m. at Goodale Park Shelterhouse, 120 W. Goodale St., to kick off a citywide cleanup!

In partnership with Keep Columbus Beautiful, Councilmember Emmanuel Remy is hosting the fourth annual Cleaner Columbus Citywide Cleanup—a community-wide effort to raise awareness about littering. All cleanup supplies will be provided.

Register your team

Food Waste Prevention

Did you know the average family throws away $2,000 worth of food each year? When food goes to the landfill, it creates powerful climate-changing gases. Instead of wasting food, Columbus residents can drop off their food scraps for free at seven convenient locations across the city, plus both Waste and Reuse Convenience Centers. Free collection buckets are available while supplies last! Learn more at columbus.gov/foodwaste.

City of Columbus Employees Clean Up 17,000 Pounds of Litter!

Hundreds of City of Columbus employees stepped up this month to make a significant impact in our communities during the biannual Citywide Employee Cleanup Day! Armed with gloves, bags, and a passion for a cleaner city, they collectively removed over 17,000 pounds of litter from our streets, parks, and neighborhoods. Their hard work is a testament to our commitment to keeping Columbus beautiful and sets a powerful example of civic pride. Together, we've made a significant impact on reducing litter.

KickButt 2025 Recap

KickButt Columbus 2025 was a massive success. Volunteers collected 58,610 pounds of litter across the city—11,930 pounds more than the total collected last year.

This incredible achievement wouldn’t have been possible without the passion and dedication of our amazing volunteers. You showed up, rolled up your sleeves, and made a real impact. Your commitment to keeping Columbus clean and beautiful is truly inspiring.

A huge THANK YOU to everyone who participated—your efforts are making our city a better, brighter place for all!

item.title: KickButt Columbus! 2025
item.description:
Are you ready to KickButt?

Cigarette butts are the most littered item in America, but it’s not the only litter that harms our community. When paper, bottles, cans and other trash litter our city streets, the debris eventually travels into our storm drains and contaminates our waterways.

Keep Columbus Beautiful fights back against litter. Kickbutt Columbus! is our annual cleanup event along the city’s highway ramps to collect litter and raise awareness about the environmental hazards of tossed cigarette butts. 

Join hundreds of Keep Columbus Beautiful volunteers on Saturday, March 22, to stomp out litter along city ramps. We will meet at 10 a.m. at Wolfe Park Shelter House, 105 Park Dr, Columbus, 43209.

Please register online, email us with any questions at keepcolumbusbeautiful@columbus.gov, or call at 614-645-2421. 

For more information on Keep Columbus Beautiful and our upcoming events, follow our social media platforms including Facebook and Instagram.

item.title: February 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
KickButt Columbus! —Let’s Take Action!

Cigarette butts are the most littered item in America, but it’s not the only litter that harms our community. When paper, bottles, cans and other trash litter our city streets, the debris eventually travels into storm drains and contaminates our waterways.

Keep Columbus Beautiful fights back against litter. Kickbutt Columbus! is our annual cleanup event along many city highway ramps to collect litter and raise awareness about the environmental hazards of tossed cigarette butts.

Join hundreds of Keep Columbus Beautiful volunteers on Saturday, March 22, to stomp out litter along highway ramps. We will meet at 10 a.m. at Wolfe Park Shelter House, 105 Park Dr., Columbus, 43209

Register here

  1. Recycle ♻️Sending a Valentine’s Day card? Choose recyclable paper and skip non-recyclable materials like glitter, confetti, and metallic wrap.
  2. Compost 🌱When your Valentine’s Day flowers start to fade, give them new life by composting them instead of tossing them in the trash.
  3. Reduce Litter 🚮Host your own cleanup and help keep Columbus beautiful! Need litter grabbers, bags, or gloves? Sign up for a supply pickup today.

Mayor Andrew J. Ginther announced that Columbus has secured an additional $100,000 from Bloomberg Philanthropies to continue the Youth Climate Action Fund in 2025. This initiative empowers young people ages 15 to 24 to create innovative climate solutions and contributes to our city’s commitment to environmental justice as part of the Columbus Climate Action Plan.

The fund will provide micro-grants for various projects, including climate education programs, community gardens, waste reduction initiatives, clean energy efforts, and more. Last year, 10 youth-led projects received funding, each working to create meaningful change in our city.

We encourage young Columbus residents to submit their ideas and proposals for funding. Applications are now open and will be accepted on a rolling basis until funds are depleted. item.title: January 2025 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
Last year, the dedicated efforts of Keep Columbus Beautiful volunteers and supporters have transformed our community for the better:

  • 💵 Economic Impact: Generating an impressive $787,214 worth of community value through cleanup, education, and beautification initiatives.
  • 🤝 Volunteers: An incredible 10,420 individuals joined forces to give back to their city.
  • 🕒 Volunteer Hours: They contributed over 24,630 hours of hard work and passion.
  • 🏡 Areas Adopted: The Adopt-An-Area program cared for and revitalized 24 neighborhoods and public spaces.
  • 📚 Education Events: With 71 events, we’ve empowered thousands with knowledge about sustainability, recycling, and the importance of a clean environment.
  • 🗑️ Litter Removed: A staggering 418,810 pounds of litter were removed from our streets, parks, and waterways, making Columbus cleaner and healthier for all.

Every bag of trash picked up, every area adopted, and every hour volunteered reflects our collective pride and commitment to a more beautiful Columbus. Thank you!

Congratulations to Our Award Winners

On Saturday, January 11, we hosted the annual Keep Columbus Beautiful Volunteer Appreciation Event to celebrate the volunteers keeping our community clean and green. These groups and individuals dedicated countless hours to litter cleanup initiatives, transforming our streets, parks, and public spaces. Through their hard work, they have beautified our surroundings and instilled a sense of pride and environmental stewardship within our community.

Partner of the Year: Carolyn Turner – Carolyn has shown tireless dedication as the site manager for FLOW at the ODNR Sawmill Wetland Education Center, organizing countless volunteer events and caring for the environment despite many challenges.

Volunteer Group of the Year: Adena Brook Community – This group’s consistent efforts to clean and restore Overbrook Ravine and surrounding areas in Clintonville have impacted the environment and the community.

Adopt-An-Area Partner of the Year: Highland West Civic Association—This group has taken on the area from West Broad Street to Interstate 70, maintaining and improving it yearly with its commitment to cleanliness and community pride.

Volunteer of the Year: Shirley Marshall – As President of the East Hampton Block Watch, Shirley has led consistent cleanups and outreach events, showing incredible resilience and commitment to her neighborhood even without a formal board.

Volunteer Youth Group of the Year: CDC Bear Cats – This enthusiastic group of young volunteers has shown dedication by organizing weekly cleanups and improving their community with consistent efforts and leadership.

Please join me in congratulating all of our winners, and thank you to everyone for your dedication to making Columbus a cleaner, greener place to live!

Save the Date!

KickButt Columbus! is on Saturday, March 22! Each March, we rally hundreds of volunteers for a powerful day of community service across Columbus. KickButt Columbus! is an annual spring highway ramp cleanup focused on removing the blight left behind after the winter thaw and raising awareness about the environmental impact of cigarette butt litter. With cleanups at nearly 35 exit ramps, this event is one of our most significant and most impactful of the year.

See you there

Educational Programs

Keep Columbus Beautiful offers engaging, science-based activities for K-12 students, connecting classroom learning to real-world environmental issues and solutions. The program includes three interactive educational activities that raise awareness about recycling, composting, and conservation while providing students with practical solutions for reducing waste. The curriculum is tailored to different grade levels – K-2, 3-5, 6-8, and 9-12 – with a unique focus for each:

  • K-2: Lessons introduce students to sorting waste and teach the differences between trash, recycling, and composting.
  • 3-5: Lessons expand on waste composition, going beyond basic recycling concepts and integrating math and social studies.
  • 6-12: Lessons delve into the complexities of waste streams, providing a deeper understanding of landfills and recycling systems.

All programming is offered free of charge.

item.title: May 2024 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
In April, we saw residents across Columbus come together, businesses step up, and volunteers roll up their sleeves to make a difference. Each tree planted, each piece of litter removed, and each conversation about environmental stewardship brought us closer to our shared vision of a greener, cleaner city.

Let's carry forward that energy and enthusiasm sparked during Earth Month throughout the summer. Let's continue cultivating sustainability, resilience, and beauty that defines Columbus. Our commitment to this mission is unwavering.

Columbus Litter League Returns

We are calling upon our community partners and volunteers to join the lineup to help strike out litter in neighborhoods throughout the city. Columbus Litter League is back, and registration is open! Litter League is a fun and competitive, baseball-themed litter abatement program managed by Keep Columbus Beautiful. Teams will compete in four divisions: corporations/businesses, nonprofits/faith-based organizations, community groups, and individuals.

Thanks to Huntington Bank and the Columbus Clippers, proud sponsors of the Columbus Litter League, every team player who participates in cleanups will be invited to enjoy special Litter League team nights at designated home Clippers' games this summer. The team with the most "runs" earned by collecting the most bags of litter will participate in a special wiffle ball tournament at Huntington Park. The 2024 Litter League season is June 1 through August 31. 

Register Your Team

 

Earth Month Thank You!

Wow! What an incredible achievement! Our volunteers' dedication and enthusiasm blew us away. With over 3,500 volunteers coming together, we have cleaned up our environment and demonstrated the power of collective action. Your efforts have made a monumental difference in our community. On behalf of the entire community, we extend our gratitude to all of our Earth Month volunteers for your commitment to keeping Columbus clean.

Have you seen an area in your neighborhood in need of a cleanup? Learn more and organize one here.

We’re Getting Our Butts Off the Ground

Thanks to a generous grant from Keep America Beautiful, Columbus residents will soon have a convenient and environmentally friendly way to dispose of cigarette butts.

We're excited to announce that this fall 25 designated bins will be placed in high-traffic pedestrian areas and near businesses to make it easy to recycle your cigarettes responsibly and not toss them on the ground. Cigarette butts are the most littered item in the U.S. The filters don't break down naturally and, when discarded on the ground, they leach toxins into the soil and our waterways.

It's time to put cigarette butts where they belong! What for Keep Columbus Beautiful updated on the butt bin locations.

Learn More

Teaching Environmental Stewardship

Did you know that Keep Columbus Beautiful offers engaging and informative education workshops tailored for students from kindergarten through 12th grade? These classroom workshops are designed to empower our youth with knowledge and skills in environmental stewardship and community involvement.

Our comprehensive workshops provide insights into an array of topics, including the impact of litter on wildlife, effective strategies for waste reduction, the issue of plastic pollution, and the importance of practicing the three R's: reduce, reuse, and recycle.

Through interactive lessons and hands-on activities, students delve into sustainability, learning practical ways to make a positive difference in their community and beyond. From understanding the lifecycle of materials to exploring innovative solutions for environmental challenges, our workshops ignite a passion for conservation and inspire action.

Join us in nurturing the next generation of environmental leaders through Keep Columbus Beautiful's education programs.

Register Your Class

item.title: April 2024 News and Updates from Keep Columbus Beautiful
item.description:
Welcome to Earth Month! As April unfolds, we have an opportunity to reflect on our collective responsibility toward our planet. At Keep Columbus Beautiful, Earth Month holds a special significance. It is a reminder of our mission to foster environmental stewardship and promote sustainable practices within our community.

Throughout this month, we invite you to join us in taking action to safeguard our environment. Whether participating in a community cleanup, planting trees, starting a composting initiative, or simply making eco-friendly choices in your daily life, every action contributes to our planet's greater good, no matter how small.

Together, let's commit to being mindful stewards of our environment and leaving a sustainability legacy for future generations.

Happy Earth Month!

Celebrate Earth Month

This is our absolute favorite time of year. Throughout April, we're inviting all Columbus residents to join us in embracing the spirit of Earth Month. Whether you're passionate about recycling, reducing your carbon footprint, supporting local green initiatives, or simply enjoying the great outdoors, there's something to get involved in for everyone!

From tree plantings and park cleanups to workshops on composting and renewable energy, there are countless ways to make a positive impact on our environment and inspire others to do the same.

Find an event near you

Cleaner Columbus Citywide Cleanup

We want to express our gratitude to every one of our volunteers who picked up litter around our community on April 6th for the third annual Cleaner Columbus Cleanup. Thanks to their hard work, our streets, parks, and neighborhoods are now cleaner and more beautiful places for everyone to enjoy. Their willingness to give their time and energy to this cause is inspiring. It serves as a shining example of the positive impact that individuals can make when they come together for a common goal. Seeing such a strong sense of community spirit among us is heartwarming. Their actions not only clean our environment but also remind us all of the importance of working together to create a better world for future generations.

National Volunteer Month

April is also #NationalVolunteerMonth! We are grateful for the support from our community members. Your volunteer role is more than cleaning up litter and beautifying neighborhoods—it's about inspiring others to take action. Our mission relies on your partnership, and we simply couldn't accomplish it without you.

Are you volunteering with us this month? Share and tag us in your photos!

If you haven't volunteered, celebrate with us this month and get involved by using the link below.

Volunteer with us

COSI Science Festival

The COSI Science Festival helps build a diverse STEAM workforce and close the STEAM skills gap by exposing individuals to science and technology where they live, learn, and lounge. This year, the COSI Science Festival is May 1 – 4, 2024. Events will be held throughout Ohio from May 1 through 3, will be three days of events throughout Ohio, and the Big Science Celebration will be held at COSI on May 4, 2024, from 11a.m. to 5 p.m.

Join Keep Columbus Beautiful at the COSI Science Festival Community Event on Friday, May 3, 2024, from 5:00 pm to 7:00 pm at the city's Refuse Collection Alum Creek station at 2100 Alum Creek Dr., as we embark on a mission to turn 'trash' into treasure, starting with upcycling used paper into 'new' paper for reuse. Please note that space is limited, and registration is required for attendance.

Register Here

Cleaner Columbus Youth Grants

The Cleaner Columbus Youth Grants, a vital part of the broader Cleaner Columbus program, are designed to enhance the cleanliness and environmental quality of the Columbus area. By engaging and educating young people, this grant plays a significant role in fostering a sense of responsibility and promoting ecological awareness among the youth, making their participation invaluable.

These grants of $500 each are open to youth-related organizations, such as school booster and church groups, who complete a Keep Columbus Beautiful-approved cleanup. We encourage you to apply. A single organization may be awarded grants three times during each funding round, to earn a maximum of $1,500.

Apply Here

Adopt an Area

During Earth Month, we're reminded of the importance of giving back to our planet and ensuring its health and vitality for future generations. If you, your family, business, or organization want to make a positive impact, we encourage you to consider our Adopt-An-Area program.

Our Adopt-An-Area program is crucial to maintaining the cleanliness and beauty of our streets and public spaces throughout Columbus. Participating groups are responsible for caring for designated areas and keeping them free of litter and debris.

As a participating group, you'll receive all the necessary cleanup supplies, project guidance, and assistance with trash collection from Keep Columbus Beautiful.

Learn More
